text: To glean is to pick up facts bit by bit from small clues. Here, Bell could tell things about patients just by looking at them.
To implore is to beg someone very seriously. Here, fans begged Doyle to pass their letters to Holmes.
To scrutinise is to look at something very closely, hunting for details. Here, Holmes and Bell studied tiny things like a scratch or some ash.
Deduction means reasoning from clues you can see to a conclusion you cannot see. Here, it was Holmes's main method.
Forensics is using science to examine evidence about a crime or accident. Here, the book is of interest to people who like that subject.
Here the writers were begging Doyle to send their letters on to Holmes, as if he were a real person.
To forward a letter means to send it on to someone else. Here, fans wanted Doyle to pass their letters to the detective.
To investigate is to look into something carefully to find out the facts. Here, some fans wanted Holmes to look into their neighbours.
To plead is to ask in a desperate, emotional way. Here, some people begged for help finding a missing person.
An obituary is a short article telling about a person's life after they have died. Here, newspapers wrote them for Holmes, a made-up man.
Mourning bands are black cloth strips worn on an arm to show sadness about a death. Here, some people wore them for Holmes.
Actual means real, not imagined. Here, Holmes was not an actual person.
To portray a character is to play or show them, such as an actor does. Here, Holmes has been shown on screen about 250 times.
This is a famous organization that keeps track of record-setting things, such as the tallest person or the most-filmed character.
Based on means built from something real. Here, Holmes was made up using a real man, Joseph Bell.
A surgeon is a doctor who treats people by operating on their bodies. Here, Bell was a Scottish surgeon.
A clerk is someone who does office jobs like keeping notes and records. Here, young Doyle worked as Bell's helper.
A medical historian studies how doctors and medicine worked in the past. Here, that is Lindsey Fitzharris's job.
Forgotten means no longer remembered. Here, Bell's story had been mostly lost until the new book.
Exceptional means unusually good. Here, Bell was an exceptional man.
A diagnosis is a doctor's decision about what illness a patient has. Here, Bell was famous for his.
Preternaturally means to a degree that seems beyond normal. Here, Bell noticed more than most people could.
Observant means good at noticing things. Here, Bell noticed small details on people.
Patients are people being treated by a doctor. Here, Bell studied them before they spoke.
A callus is a thick, hard patch of skin from rubbing or hard work. Here, they showed which job a person did.
A carpenter is a person who builds things from wood.
A mason is a worker who builds with stone or brick.
Gait is the way a person walks. Here, it helped tell a soldier from a sailor.
An ailment is an illness, usually a small one. Here, shoes could hint at one.
A clay pipe is a small pipe made of baked clay that people once used to smoke tobacco.
An amphitheatre is a round room with rising rows of seats around a stage. Here, students watched Bell work like a show.
An infirmary is a hospital. Here, it is the big hospital in Edinburgh where Bell taught.
Electrifying means very exciting. Here, Bell's lessons felt like thrilling theatre.
A police surgeon is a doctor who helps police understand injuries and deaths in crime cases.
A criminal investigation is the police work of finding out who committed a crime and how.
Painstakingly means with great care, step by slow step.
A post-mortem examination, also called an autopsy, is a doctor's careful check of a body after death to learn what caused it.
To discharge a gun means to fire it. Here, the question was whether a gun went off by accident.
A cadaver is a dead human body, used for study.
Here, powder means gunpowder, the material inside a bullet that makes it shoot out.
A protagonist is the main character of a story.
An investigator is a person who looks into a crime or mystery to find the facts.
To rely on chance is to count on luck instead of skill. Here, Holmes solved cases using his brain.
A blunder is a silly or careless mistake. Here, many old detective stories needed criminals to make them.
A coincidence is when two things happen together by luck, with no reason. Here, Doyle found them annoying in mysteries.
A trope is a common idea that shows up again and again in stories.
A genre is a kind of book or film, such as mystery or fantasy.
Analysis means studying something by breaking it into parts.
Seemingly means in a way that looks true but may not be. Here, the details looked minor but were not.
Minor means small or not very important.
A tallow candle is an old-fashioned candle made from animal fat.
A candle that is guttering burns weakly and flickers before going out.
Trivialities are small things that seem unimportant.
Genius is unusual, brilliant ability.
To uncover something is to find or reveal what was hidden.
To fascinate is to hold someone's interest strongly.
True crime is a kind of story about real crimes and how they were solved.
Having a strong stomach means being able to read or see gross things without feeling sick.
The creative process is the way a person comes up with and builds a new idea or work of art.
To draw on something is to use it as a source. Here, Doyle used real people for his stories.
To transmute is to change one thing completely into another. Here, Doyle turned real people into something new.

forms: the bones on which to put the flesh
text: This means real people were the basic frame, and Doyle added the details to make full characters.
An idiosyncrasy is an odd habit or trait that belongs to one person.
An Inverness cape is a long coat with a cape over the shoulders, once worn in Scotland.
A magnifying glass is a lens that makes small things look bigger.
A trait is a quality that makes up part of someone's character.
Enduring means lasting a long time.
To dedicate a book to someone is to put their name in it as an honor.
An association is a link in people's minds between two things.
Here, a curse means something that brings trouble even though it seems like good luck.
To pester is to bother someone again and again.
Emotionally detached means cool and not showing feelings. People wrongly thought Bell was this way.
To confess is to admit something, often something hard to say.
To be haunted by something is to be followed by it and unable to escape it.
A nuisance is something or someone that keeps annoying you.
